skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

version.changelog:
- Removed the file: skill-card.md
- No other functional or logic changes in this version.

llm.summary: The skill is purpose-related but Review-worthy because it uploads media to configured services while silently creating or reusing local identity and token state for account-linked history access.

dimensions.detail: The scripts inspect workspace/environment identity context, read data/smyx-api-key.txt, create workspace data storage, upload local files or submit remote URLs, and the active dev config overrides public endpoints with private 192.168.1.234 HTTP URLs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No destructive install hook or background installer was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though one requirements file appears to contain an install typo for yaml==6.0.3.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions use broad default triggers for uploaded frog media and automatic keyword-based history queries, and direct the agent not to ask for or show identity values while the scripts silently resolve or create an identity.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates/reuses a local SQLite user database and stores token/open_token values, then attaches X-Access-Token, X-Api-Key, and Authorization headers to outbound requests.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Frog skin moisture analysis is coherent with image/video input, cloud analysis, report links, and history reports, but the artifact also includes generic video-analysis components, automatic account provisioning, and token-backed history access that exceed the narrow headline purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with frog images or videos leaving the local machine, account-linked report history being queried from a cloud service, and a local workspace database storing identity tokens. The private dev HTTP endpoints and silent identity provisioning should be fixed or explicitly documented before normal user installation.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The unvalidated getattr filters exist in the generic DAO, but I did not find a user-facing path that exposes arbitrary filter keys; this is a code-quality risk, not a driver of the verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: The manifest has no structured permission declaration while the artifact clearly uses shell-invoked scripts, local file reads/writes, network calls, environment identity values, and persistent storage.
[TP4] unexpected: Cloud analysis and history are disclosed in the body, but silent identity creation/reuse, token handling, and account-linked report retrieval are materially broader than the front-matter description.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The main wrapper uses the frog scene code, but bundled generic video-analysis code and account/auth utilities broaden the skill beyond a simple visual moisture assessor.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifact-backed concerns about automatic history listing, remote URL ingestion, reading workspace identity material, and storing tokens are valid Review concerns.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The --export-env-only flag is advertised but not implemented before identity resolution or analysis flow, and generic video CLI text conflicts with the frog-specific presentation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Automatic default processing and broad history keywords are too loose for a skill that performs credentialed cloud calls and can return account-linked records.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Local file contents can be read and uploaded, or a remote URL can be forwarded to the backend, without a runtime confirmation step in the script.
[E1] unexpected: The code posts openId/mobile/source to a login/provisioning endpoint; remote identity provisioning may be needed for the service but is under-scoped and silent for this purpose.
[P2] unexpected: A zero-width character is present in SKILL.md, but it appears inside an ordinary safety-warning line and does not by itself show hidden malicious instructions.
[YR4] unexpected: The metadata is overlong and operational, and its narrow headline under-discloses some account/network behavior; this supports Review but not a malicious finding.
